players.product: CMP pads, cleans & slurries and lithography ancillary materials for leading-edge logic/memory (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: First earnings call as a stand-alone public company. Q4 2025 net sales were $1.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year, even though $40 million of sales shifted from Q4 into Q3 because of the spin-related IT transition; adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA was $349 million and adjusted pro forma EPS $0.82. Full-year 2025 net sales grew 10% to $4.75 billion (organic +10%, the seventh consecutive quarter of organic growth), with adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of $1.4 billion (29.5% margin), adjusted pro forma EPS of $3.35 and adjusted pro forma free cash flow of $706 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 net sales $1.2 billion (up 8%); adj. EBITDA $349 million; adj. EPS $0.82; FY2025 net sales $4.75 billion; adj. EBITDA $1.4 billion (29.5%); adj. EPS $3.35; FCF $706 million

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor Technologies grew organic sales 8% in 2025, driven mostly by semi fab consumables; AI/HPC demand drove double-digit growth in advanced nodes and advanced packaging, with ongoing improvement in mature nodes and NAND. The advanced logic and high-bandwidth memory business grew mid-teens, moving toward the 45% to 50% advanced node exposure target from Investor Day. Segment margins came in in the mid-30s, with incremental R&D and engineering investment to support the scale-up of advanced nodes.
quarterly_data.figure: Semi organic sales 8% (2025); advanced logic + HBM grew mid-teens; advanced node exposure target 45% to 50%; segment margin mid-30s

quarterly_data.signal: In October Qnity introduced its Emblem CMP pad platform, which addresses the planarization requirements of the most advanced chips including N3 and N2 Logic and HBM3 and 4 memory; customer feedback was described as outstanding. CMP advanced cleans and slurries are also growing strongly across leading-edge logic and memory. Customers are scaling 3-nanometer and starting early production of 2-nanometer, and memory is moving to next-generation DRAM, HBM and higher layer count NAND.

Fab utilization outlook for 2026: advanced logic rising from the high 70s at year-end 2025 to low to mid-80s; mature logic continuing to improve toward the mid- to high 70s (a modest recovery tied to the memory market); DRAM rising from mid-80s in 2025 to high 80s; NAND reaching the upper 70s or low 80s. With strong utilization and accelerating capacity expansion, customers are prioritizing supply security.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced logic high 70s to low to mid-80s; mature logic mid- to high 70s; DRAM mid-80s to high 80s; NAND upper 70s or low 80s (2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Initial full-year 2026 guidance: net sales $4.97 billion to $5.17 billion (implied midpoint a little over 6.5% growth), adjusted operating EBITDA $1.465 billion to $1.575 billion, adjusted EPS $3.55 to $3.95 and adjusted free cash flow $450 million to $550 million, anchored on MSI wafer starts growing about mid-single digits plus content outperformance. Q1 2026 net sales expected to grow high single digits sequentially with a margin profile similar to Q4. The high end depends on customers bringing new advanced-node capacity online; the low end would reflect memory-market constraints causing significant demand destruction.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales $4.97 billion to $5.17 billion; adj. EBITDA $1.465 billion to $1.575 billion; adj. EPS $3.55 to $3.95; adj. FCF $450 million to $550 million; MSI mid-single digits; Q1 sequential growth high single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and customer design wins: Qnity added new capacity in all semi businesses over the last 3 years and plans elevated capex of 9% of sales in 2026 (local-for-local footprint, IT independence and transformation initiatives) before returning to a normal run rate of roughly 6% of net sales. In 2025 it secured Process of Record (POR) wins across every line of business, early design selections that typically scale into commercial production over the next 2 to 3 years.
quarterly_data.figure: capex 9% of sales (2026), then roughly 6%; POR wins scale over 2 to 3 years

quarterly_data.signal: China grew high single digits in 2025, better than expected, and accounted for just over 30% of total sales; the rest of Asia and the Americas both grew double digits, with similar dynamics expected in 2026. In the second half of 2025, Chinese customers normalized to buying on performance, quality and supply reliability.
quarterly_data.figure: China just over 30% of total sales; China growth high single digits (2025)

players.product: CMP pads & slurries, photoresists, advanced-packaging laminates (ex-DuPont Electronics)

quarterly_data.signal: Interconnect Solutions (ICS) grew organic sales 12% in 2025, led by advanced packaging, advanced interconnects and thermal management, which each increased more than 20% for the year on several wins at leading fabs and OEMs. Segment adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA margin was just over 25%, an expansion of over 175 basis points. Advanced interconnect growth comes from the shift to high layer count and HDI circuit boards with finer lines and spaces for data centers.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging, advanced interconnects and thermal management each up more than 20% (2025); ICS margin just over 25% (expansion of over 175 basis points)

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging solutions represented approximately 10% of Qnity net sales in 2025 and draw on both the semi and ICS segments. CMP pads, slurries and cleans are used in advanced packaging and are one of the fastest-growing areas of that portfolio: planarization is critical for copper-to-copper bonding in traditional formats and in hybrid bonding as structures get taller and more complex. New copper interconnect chemistry is being broadly adopted by key fab and OSAT customers.
quarterly_data.figure: advanced packaging approximately 10% of net sales (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 growth in advanced packaging and thermal materials is gated by customer capacity, not demand: ICS benefited from available capacity in 2025, and 2026 growth rates are largely driven by the incremental capacity customers bring online ("it's not a matter of demand. It's really a matter of how fast can we get that incremental capacity online"). New thermal pads, liquid gap fillers and phase change materials are seeing rapid adoption by cloud service providers and OEMs. ICS is expected to grow somewhat faster than the semi segment in 2026, and Q1 2026 shows notable strength in ICS.
